title: Companies Act, 2013 — Section 453 (Punishment for improper use of 'Limited' or 'Private Limited')

content.overview: A person or persons who trade or carry on business under a name of which 'Limited' or 'Private Limited' is the last word, without being duly incorporated with limited liability, is punishable with fine.
content.glance: A person or persons who trade or carry on business under a name of which 'Limited' or 'Private Limited' is the last word, without being duly incorporated with limited liability, is punishable with fine.
content.study: Companies Act, 2013 — Section 453 (Punishment for improper use of 'Limited' or 'Private Limited'). A person or persons who trade or carry on business under a name of which 'Limited' or 'Private Limited' is the last word, without being duly incorporated with limited liability, is punishable with fine. Apply only the conditions, approvals, filings and penalties stated in the section. A rule made under the Act cannot contradict the section. Not a verified closure.

sections.heading: Rule
sections.body: A person or persons who trade or carry on business under a name of which 'Limited' or 'Private Limited' is the last word, without being duly incorporated with limited liability, is punishable with fine.

sections.heading: Explanation
sections.body: The section protects the public from a false appearance of limited liability. An incorporated company using its registered name is outside it.
